plan: [ One-shot second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it ensures you win exactly when the second-highest bid is below your value and never pay above your value. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest exceeds your value. No history to exploit and values are redrawn, so no strategic signaling value. With value $40 and $0.1 increments, bid exactly 40 to maximize expected profit. ]

[ It's a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values (0–49). The dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: my bid determines only whether I win, not the price I pay (which is the second-highest bid). Shading risks losing profitable wins without lowering payment when I would win. With value 13 and no informative history (single round), bidding my true value maximizes expected profit in this and any repeated setting with similar rules. ]

[ This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy is truthful bidding: bid my value. By bidding 17, I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below 17 and pay that amount, maximizing expected profit. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks paying above my value. One round; no history effects. ]
